macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks face sharp pullback as oil prices surge
items.summary: Major U.S. indexes were pressured by rising oil prices and reports of planned U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran. Nasdaq futures fell about 1.7% and S&P 500 futures about 1.0%, while the Dow held up better.[1][2]

items.title: Prior session closes higher before futures reverse
items.summary: The Nasdaq Composite gained 1.05% to 26,702.86, the S&P 500 rose 0.58% to 7,757.17, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average increased 0.69% to 52,856.09 before overnight futures turned lower.[3]

items.title: Meta shares slide despite earnings and revenue beat
items.summary: Meta reported third-quarter revenue of $64.6 billion and adjusted earnings per share of $3.83, both above expectations. Shares nevertheless fell as investors focused on increased capital-spending requirements.[4][5]

items.title: Tesla falls after cutting capital-expenditure outlook
items.summary: Tesla reported third-quarter revenue of $28.05 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.48, slightly beating earnings expectations but narrowly missing revenue forecasts. The company cut its full-year capital-expenditure forecast to $20 billion from $25 billion, pressuring the stock.[4]

items.title: Lam Research and IBM weigh on technology sector
items.summary: Lam Research shares dropped about 8% despite strong year-over-year growth after its forward guidance failed to exceed elevated expectations. IBM shares fell about 7% even after beating quarterly estimates, as investors questioned the growth outlook.[2]

items.title: Defense and consumer companies outperform
items.summary: Lockheed Martin rose more than 4% after reporting results above consensus and raising guidance. Procter & Gamble gained about 3% after beating earnings expectations and increasing its sales-growth forecast.[2]

items.title: Fed policy remains the key market driver
items.summary: Federal Reserve policy continued to be identified as the primary swing factor for the Dow and broader U.S. equities, while U.S. initial jobless claims were among the key economic releases scheduled for the session.[6][7]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Morgan Stanley Bitcoin ETF receives $93.9 million inflow
items.summary: Morgan Stanley’s MSBT Bitcoin ETF received 1,100 BTC from Coinbase Prime, worth approximately $93.89 million, reportedly its largest single inflow since launch.

items.title: OCC issues final stablecoin rule under GENIUS Act
items.summary: The U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency issued final standards for stablecoin issuers under its supervision ahead of the GENIUS Act’s planned effective date in January 2027.

items.title: Solana activates Alpenglow consensus upgrade
items.summary: Solana validators activated the Alpenglow upgrade on the live network, retiring TowerBFT, the consensus mechanism used since the network launched in 2020.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum post modest gains
items.summary: Bitcoin rose about 0.87% over 24 hours to roughly $82,004, while Ether gained 0.31% to approximately $2,402, according to OKX market data.

items.title: BCH surges after CME futures announcement
items.summary: Bitcoin Cash briefly jumped about 30% above $340, touching approximately $358, after CME Group announced planned BCH and Uniswap futures launches pending regulatory approval.

items.title: NEAR rises 5% amid ecosystem developments
items.summary: NEAR gained approximately 5% to $5.29 as AI-related staking surpassed one million tokens, Near Business launched, and Near Intents volume reached $35.6 billion.

items.title: Crypto projects urge SEC to clarify digital-commodity rules
items.summary: The Stellar Development Foundation joined Hedera, Aptos, Ava Labs, Cardano and Chainlink in urging the SEC to clarify the classification of digital commodities under proposed crypto regulations.

items.title: LayerZero expands ZRO token buybacks
items.summary: LayerZero reportedly bought more than 162,000 ZRO tokens, bringing cumulative buybacks to approximately 2.538 million tokens valued at about $5.4 million.

items.title: Google Cloud to discontinue blockchain node services
items.summary: Google Cloud said its Blockchain Node Engine and Blockchain RPC services will shut down on December 15, 2026, prompting customers to arrange migrations.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Recursive releases Flint open-weight coding model
items.summary: Recursive released Flint, an Apache 2.0 local coding model with 40 billion total parameters and 2.5 billion active parameters. The company reports 74.2% on SWE-bench Verified and more than 125 tokens per second on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro.[2]

items.title: OpenAI models arrive on Google Cloud
items.summary: OpenAI announced plans to make its latest large language models available through Google Cloud’s Model Garden, giving enterprise customers access to OpenAI models alongside Google’s Gemini and Anthropic’s Claude.[2]

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Duet proactive agent
items.summary: Anthropic announced Claude Duet, a standalone proactive-agent application powered by Claude Opus 5.5. The product is positioned alongside emerging agent applications from Meta and OpenAI.[3]

items.title: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer inference engine
items.summary: DeepSeek released DeepInfer, the production inference engine behind V4.1 Flash, along with a companion protocol-conversion library. The release supports NVIDIA SM100 and Huawei Ascend 950 hardware.[5]

items.title: Google DeepMind and Cambridge report autonomous mathematical discovery
items.summary: A joint Google DeepMind–University of Cambridge paper describes a Gemini-based AI agent that autonomously discovers new mathematical rules, highlighting progress in AI-assisted research.[4]

items.title: Meta reports more than 10 million Muse AI users
items.summary: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said the Muse AI agent app has surpassed 10 million users, with shopping identified as one of the leading activities.[8]

items.title: Lanxin unveils RISC-V AI inference supernode
items.summary: Lanxin Computing launched a supernode based on its 48-core LX500 RISC-V inference chip, which integrates general-purpose computing and a 75 TOPS INT8 AI engine on one die.[2]

items.title: Industry shifts toward non-LLM foundation models
items.summary: New model categories are gaining attention, including tabular foundation models, decision-focused systems, and code-execution models that operate inside running programs. The trend reflects growing interest in specialized AI beyond text-generating large language models.[10]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: EA shuts down BioWare and cancels next Mass Effect
items.summary: Electronic Arts announced the closure of BioWare and cancellation of its next Mass Effect project as part of a broader restructuring affecting about 400 employees. EA said it will focus on fewer major franchises, including Battlefield, Apex Legends, EA Sports FC, Marvel’s Iron Man, and the next Star Wars Jedi game.

items.title: Indonesia gaming industry projected to add $3.3 billion by 2030
items.summary: A Tencent and Access Partnership report projects that Indonesia’s gaming industry could contribute up to $3.3 billion in economic value and support 476,600 jobs by 2030 under an accelerated-growth scenario. The report calls for more financing and stronger support for local studios and intellectual property.

items.title: Whitemoon Games launches Broken Ranks worldwide on Android
items.summary: Polish developer Whitemoon Games announced the worldwide Android release of its free-to-play isometric MMORPG Broken Ranks.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Bose acquires Skullcandy
items.summary: Bose announced the acquisition of rival headphone and speaker maker Skullcandy on October 21. Financial terms were not disclosed, and Skullcandy will remain a separate brand within Bose’s consumer audio division.

items.title: Electronic Arts shuts down BioWare and cancels next Mass Effect
items.summary: Electronic Arts is reportedly closing BioWare after more than three decades and canceling the studio’s next Mass Effect game, marking a major change for one of the game industry’s best-known role-playing franchises.

items.title: Tesla begins Optimus robot production as profit falls
items.summary: Tesla has started production of its Optimus humanoid robot in California, while the company reported a 43% decline in profit, highlighting continued pressure to commercialize new businesses beyond electric vehicles.

items.title: Tesla says Cybercab sales will begin by year-end
items.summary: Tesla said it plans to begin selling its Cybercab autonomous vehicle by the end of 2026, adding a firm sales target to its broader self-driving and robotaxi strategy.

items.title: Tesla and SpaceX create committees to evaluate possible merger
items.summary: Tesla and SpaceX have established independent-director committees to examine a potential combination of the two companies, according to Elon Musk.

items.title: Automattic begins layoffs after leadership upheaval
items.summary: WordPress.com owner Automattic has begun layoffs following board turmoil and executive departures, adding to recent uncertainty around the company’s strategy and governance.

items.title: Blacksmith Software raises $66 million at $1 billion valuation
items.summary: Continuous-integration startup Blacksmith Software raised $66 million in a Series C funding round that values the company at $1 billion.
